title: Monthly and six-month ENSO directions had opposite signs in 9 of 88 intervals from 1980 to 2024
abstract: We tested whether six-month endpoint geometry gives the same direction as the monthly path in a Pacific volume-temperature state. We used fixed NOAA GODAS basin warm water volume and ERSSTv5 Nino 3.4 monthly means. March and September anchors gave 88 intervals from March 1980 to March 2024. The endpoint determinant and the sum of six monthly determinants had opposite signs in 9 intervals, or 10.23%. A conditional 95 percent three-year block interval was 3.41% to 18.18%. Three-month smoothing gave the same count. Removing paths with an endpoint norm below 0.5 reduced the count to 3 of 73. Both measures had positive mean direction. An exact identity shows that their difference is twice the signed area between the monthly path and its chord. Thus the difference has a geometric explanation and is not evidence of a new physical process. One product pair, origin choice, weak states and few dependent cycles limit the result. Original code, aggregate evidence, an independent scalar audit, source hashes and retrieval instructions support reproduction. External monthly records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Direction counts for 88 six-month intervals and sign-disagreement rates under three planned checks. Error bars are conditional 95 percent three-year block intervals. Positive direction is the volume-leading-temperature orientation.
